comparison: Both address pathological consequences of IMLECs (C77-C89). OpenEval finds the evidence comprehensive and well-supported with adequate sample sizes. Peer reviewers remain uncertain, expressing major concerns that the inflammatory impact is not adequately demonstrated and requesting graded bone marrow chimera experiments to show disease consequences when IMLEC numbers approach WT levels.

Both evaluate PRR overexpression and TLR functionality (C70-C76). OpenEval finds the data well-supported with comprehensive TLR ligand testing. Peer reviewers are uncertain, raising a critical concern that TLR overexpression may be a response to pIpC administration rather than intrinsic to IMLECs, a confounding factor not adequately addressed.

Both address interpretive conclusions about novelty and immune tolerance mechanisms (C90-C92). OpenEval finds claims logically supported but notes the 'new mechanism of immune tolerance' is somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers are uncertain, stating the manuscript over-interprets data and focuses too much on cell number regulation of self-tolerance, which is peripheral to findings.

Both evaluate the c-Myb mechanistic link (C62-C69). OpenEval finds the evidence well-established through multiple lines including rescue experiments. Peer reviewers initially supported this after rescue data was provided, but raised concerns that massive IMLEC generation following Myb deletion suggests these may be preleukemic cells, questioning physiological relevance.

Both address increased HSPCs despite reduced mature cells (C16-C17). OpenEval finds this consistent with prior reports and appropriately supported. Peer reviewers also support this finding, noting it is consistent with published literature and not challenging the observations.

Both evaluate developmental origin claims (C55-C61). OpenEval finds proliferation, apoptosis, and differentiation data convincingly rule out alternative mechanisms. Peer reviewers are uncertain, noting contradictions between LysM-Cre and mixed chimera experiments, and that LSK cells give rise mostly to granulocytes rather than IMLECs in vivo.

Both address characterization of Rptor-deficient IMLECs using multiple methods (C2-C7, C25-C39, C42). OpenEval finds characterization well-supported by complementary approaches. Peer reviewers accept the characterization as well-performed and in-depth, though requesting additional phenotypic markers and noting concerns about whether mTOR deficiency affects marker expression.

Both evaluate proliferation and apoptosis data (C50-C54). OpenEval finds the data convincingly demonstrate IMLECs are non-dividing with no survival advantage. Peer reviewers are uncertain, raising methodological concerns that comparing IMLECs to heterogeneous bone marrow populations is not appropriate, though BrdU data was provided in response.

Both address the emergence of IMLECs in Rptor-deficient mice (C1, C18-C20, C22-C23). OpenEval finds this well-documented as part of comprehensive characterization. Peer reviewers acknowledge this as interesting and well-documented, with tamoxifen-inducible data specifically provided to address polyIC confounding concerns.

Both address WT IMLEC characterization (C40-C41, C47-C49). OpenEval finds WT IMLECs show comparable features to cKO IMLECs with quantitative documentation. Peer reviewers are uncertain with major concerns from all three reviewers, noting flow cytometry shows two distinct populations that don't precisely correspond to Rptor-deficient cells, and characterization is 'not convincing' and 'mostly correlative.'

Both address IMLEC presence across multiple tissues (C43-C46). OpenEval finds phenotypic markers consistently validated across tissues. Peer reviewers are uncertain, specifically criticizing speculation about CD11chigh populations and requesting proof rather than speculation, reflecting broader concerns about WT IMLEC characterization.

OpenEval evaluated contextualization within mTOR inhibitor literature (C99-C106), finding claims appropriately contextualized though noting reliance on unpublished negative data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific literature context claims.

OpenEval evaluated background claims on immune tolerance (C11-C15), finding them well-established and appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these foundational background claims.
